items.proof_plan: The relative support inclusion for (X,X^{p-1}) and (X,X^{q-1}) maps under a cellular diagonal to support in (X,X^{p+q-1}); pair the D and E vertices by the external product and this diagonal. The two boundary identities give k(xy)=k(x)y+(-1)^{|x|}xk(y). If kx=i^{r-1}u and ky=i^{r-1}v, compatibility with i gives k(xy)=i^{r-1}(uy+(-1)^{|x|}xv), proving the Leibniz rule on the rth derived couple and independence from lifts. Products of cycles and boundaries identify E_{r+1} with H(E_r,d_r) as algebras. Forgetting support gives F^pF^q⊆F^{p+q}, and finite convergence identifies the stable quotient product with gr_F. Homotopic cellular diagonals agree from E2 onward.

items.proof_plan: Write ku for Adams's bu and H for the integral Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum. Reconstruct exactly the opening of Adams Proposition 16.6: with the generator t∈π₂(bu) fixed, the first k-invariant is a degree-three stable integral operation; Adams identifies its two possibilities as 0 and δ₂Sq², because the relevant operation group H³(H) is Z/2 generated by δ₂Sq². He then examines the third spectrum space SU: the same passage supplies both δ₂Sq²≠0 in H⁶(K(Z,3);Z) and H⁶(SU;Z)=0, forcing the invariant to be the nonzero generator. Finally Adams uses the Bott cofiber S²∧bu→bu→H and its long exact mod-two cohomology sequence; the boundary sends the suspended fundamental class to β₂Sq² of the fundamental class, fixing the generator rather than only its nonvanishing. Under the local Bockstein and Steenrod conventions δ₂Sq² is β_ZSq²ρ₂. Adams also states that every representing space has this same stable operation, so the fixed Bott maps transport the normalization. The H³, H⁶(K(Z,3);Z), and H⁶(SU;Z) facts are used only as facts explicitly supplied in that proof; no independent computation of them is asserted here.

items.statement: Assume AC. Write ku for Adams's connective complex K-theory spectrum bu and fix its Bott generator t∈π₂(ku). Its first k-invariant is the nonzero degree-three stable integral operation δ₂Sq²=β_ZSq²ρ₂. The same stable operation occurs in every representing space, so the fixed Bott translates carry this normalization.

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the bundle model of complex K-theory and its representing spectrum.
items.proof_plan: First identify theories, rather than silently changing models. For a based finite CW quotient Y=X/A, the finite-rank complement theorem writes every virtual bundle as [E]−[epsilon^N]. Stable complex-bundle classification sends this to the component rank(E)−N of a map Y→Z×BU; adding a trivial summand does not change the stabilized classifying map, while a homotopy gives the corresponding stable bundle isomorphism. Thus Grothendieck's common-summand relation proves, in both directions, the natural isomorphism reduced K^0(Y)≅[Y,Z×BU]. May constructs the Bott-compatible Omega-prespectrum KU with KU_(2i)=Z×BU and KU_(2i+1)=U; its adjoint structure equivalences are the loop equivalence and Bott equivalence. Therefore the degree-zero identification, suspension adjunction, and the proved natural Bott maps give, inductively in both directions, natural isomorphisms KU^n(X,A)≅K^n(X,A) in every degree. Because both connecting maps are obtained from the same quotient/cofiber map followed by suspension, these isomorphisms commute with relative maps and connectors, so they identify the locally constructed skeletal K-AHSS with the KU skeletal exact couple. Next use Adams's connective spectrum bu (modern ku) and map ku→KU: its stable homotopy is zero below zero and maps isomorphically to KU in nonnegative degrees. Bott-translate any KU coefficient row to q≤0. On the E1 cellular groups the induced map of skeletal exact couples is the wedge, over the p-cells, of ku^q(*)→KU^q(*), hence is an isomorphism throughout q≤0; the intervening odd groups vanish and the target row q−2 is still nonpositive. Naturality for theory morphisms and induction with the exact-couple local-lift formula therefore identify the E3 source, target, and d3 for ku and KU in these rows. Finally let p≥2 and represent an E3 class by an E1 cellular cocycle e. The r=3 local-lift formula gives k(e)=i²y and d3[e]=[j(y)]. In the skeletal-pair couple the two i-preimages are exactly the compatible extensions of the representing map over X^(p+1) and X^(p+2). Pulling back the first Postnikov fibration of the corresponding ku representing space, the cellular lifting-obstruction theorem says that its obstruction on each oriented (p+3)-cell is the attaching-map composite represented by j(y). Thus the skeletal d3 is exactly pullback of that representing-space Postnikov invariant, independently of the chosen lifts. For p=1, suspend the reduced class once: suspension of every skeletal-pair long exact sequence gives a termwise isomorphism of exact couples, so it commutes with the r=3 local-lift formula; the p=2 comparison desuspends to p=1. Quotienting a finite CW pair by its subcomplex and applying the same argument proves the relative case.

items.proof_plan: The displayed bidegree sends an even coefficient row under d₂ to an odd coefficient group, which is zero, so d₂=0 and E₃=E₂. First handle p=0, where the positive-degree Postnikov argument does not apply. A finite CW complex has finitely many path components. On each component X_a, every x∈H^0(X_a;Z) is the pullback of an integer along X_a→*. AHSS naturality gives d₃(x) as the pullback of d₃ on the point, whose H^3 target is zero; restriction to all components therefore gives d₃(x)=0. Instability also gives Sq²ρ₂(x)=0, so β_ZSq²ρ₂(x)=0. For p≥1, Bott-translate the coefficient row to q≤0. The preceding representability/comparison lemma identifies the local K-AHSS d₃ with the first representing-space ku Postnikov obstruction, including the p=1 suspension reduction and the finite-pair case. The connective-k-invariant lemma identifies that obstruction with β_ZSq²ρ₂. Transport back through the fixed natural Bott isomorphisms; naturality for theory morphisms makes these isomorphisms maps of skeletal exact couples. A possible global sign from the long-exact-sequence convention is immaterial because the operation has order two.

items.proof_plan: Because λ⊗_Rλ is trivial, ξ⊗_Cξ is trivial and (1+α)²=1, hence α²=-2α and α^k=(-2)^{k-1}α. Atiyah's exact sequences for successive projective skeleta identify α^k with the nonzero filtration-2k class and show that the last such class is nonzero for k=m and vanishes for k=m+1. Thus 2^mα=0 but 2^{m-1}α≠0, resolving the repeated Z/2 AHSS quotients as one cyclic group. The same exact sequences and the top integral cohomology column give the asserted odd group.

items.proof_plan: Represent x by a mod-two cocycle and choose an integral lift c. Write δc=2b, so β_Z(x) is represented by b and its reduction by b mod 2. Reducing c mod 4 gives the same quotient δc/2 mod 2 that defines the Bockstein for 0→Z/2→Z/4→Z/2→0. The published identification of that Bockstein with Sq¹ yields the formula; changing the lift changes b mod 2 by a coboundary.

items.proof_plan: Field Kunneth and the truncated projective-space rings make u²v⁴ nonzero. For z=β_Z(uv), the reduction lemma and Cartan formula give ρ_2z=Sq¹(uv)=u²v+uv². The projective-space square formula and Cartan then give Sq²(ρ_2z)=uv⁴: the possible u⁴v term vanishes on RP² and the mixed Sq¹ terms vanish. Thus Sq_Z³(z)=β_Z(uv⁴). Its reduction is Sq¹(uv⁴)=u²v⁴≠0, so the integral class itself is nonzero.

items.proof_plan: Identify BSO(2) with CP^∞ by sending an oriented real plane to its complex line. The unit-circle bundle of the universal oriented plane has the contractible stable Stiefel space as total space, so the vector-bundle Gysin sequence makes multiplication by its Euler class an isomorphism H⁰→H²; hence that Euler class is a generator. On a fiber CP^{n-1}, the restricted tautological line is classified by the standard inclusion CP^{n-1}→CP^∞. Naturality and the published integral ring calculation therefore make its Euler class a degree-two generator and its powers a basis; for n=1 the basis is just 1 and the restricted degree-two class is zero.

Integrally, unique a_i∈H^{2i}(B;Z) satisfy x^n-a_1x^{n-1}+⋯+(-1)^na_n=0, and this monic relation generates all polynomial relations.

items.proof_plan: Split off a tautological line at each finite stage using a metric, and define roots after c1 exists.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §3, splitting principle by iterated projectivization, printed pp. 208–210
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. Iterated projectivization and Hermitian complements give q:Fl(E)→B with q^*E=L_1⊕⋯⊕L_n; t_i=c_1(L_i) are the Chern roots.
items.title: Complex flag bundle and Chern roots

items.proof_plan: For R=Z or a field F_p, each projective pullback is the coefficient-of-one inclusion in the corresponding Leray–Hirsch module from the strengthened projective-bundle theorem. Compose the tower and iterate for finitely many bundles; the same construction supplies a common injection for every stated coefficient ring.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §3, splitting principle and splitting lemma, printed pp. 208–210
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. The flag projection splits q^*E into lines and has injective q^*:H^*(B;R)→H^*(Fl(E);R) for R=Z and for every field F_p. Finitely many bundles have a common such splitting space with coefficientwise injective pullback.
items.title: Complex splitting principle with integral injective pullback

items.proof_plan: Use the projective-bundle pullback square and coefficient uniqueness for naturality; on a common splitting space multiply line factors and descend by injectivity.
items.statement: Assume AC. Chern classes are pullback natural, c_1(L)=e(L_R), and c(E⊕F)=c(E)c(F), including rank-zero and stabilization conventions.
items.title: Naturality, normalization, and Whitney sum for Chern classes

items.proof_plan: Pull to a flag space, where the axioms force the product over line roots, and descend equality by injectivity.

references.locator: Chapter 23 §7, Chern-class axioms and uniqueness, printed pp. 197–200
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. The total Chern class is uniquely determined by pullback naturality, Whitney multiplication, degree-zero part one, and c(L)=1+e(L_R) on lines.
items.title: Uniqueness of Chern classes from the splitting principle

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from bundle classification and the cohomological Kunneth theorem.
items.proof_plan: Use the stable contractible Stiefel space EU(n). Its U(n)-quotient is BU(n); quotienting by the maximal torus T^n gives the complete flag bundle, and the same contractible total space identifies EU(n)/T^n with BT^n=(CP^∞)^n. The ordered tautological lines are the n coordinate universal lines. Compatible finite products of finite projective skeleta, their integral polynomial rings, and Kunneth give H^*(BT^n;Z)=Z[t_1,…,t_n]. Permutation matrices normalize T^n, permute the line factors, and cover the identity of BU(n), so every class pulled back from BU(n) is symmetric.

references.locator: Lectures 34–35, universal flag bundle, maximal torus and splitting principle, printed pp.123–132
references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.statement: Assume AC. For the universal rank-n complex bundle over BU(n), its complete flag bundle is homotopy equivalent over BU(n) to BT^n=(CP^∞)^n. Under this equivalence the Chern roots are the coordinate generators t_i and H^*(BT^n;Z)=Z[t_1,…,t_n]. The symmetric group permutes the t_i by bundle maps over BU(n), so the image of q^* is contained in the symmetric invariants.
items.title: The universal complex flag bundle is BT-n

items.proof_plan: Apply integral splitting to the universal bundle, so q^* is injective. The flag-space lemma identifies the target as Z[t_1,…,t_n] and puts the image inside its symmetric invariants. Whitney multiplication after splitting sends q^*c_i to the ith elementary symmetric polynomial e_i. Hence the image contains Z[e_1,…,e_n], while the fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials says this is the entire invariant ring. Therefore q^* identifies H^*(BU(n);Z) with Z[e_1,…,e_n], proving both generation and algebraic independence without a Gysin or finite-index shortcut.
items.statement: Assume AC. H^*(BU(n);Z)=Z[c_1,…,c_n], and restriction to BT^n sends c_i to the ith elementary symmetric polynomial in universal line roots.
items.title: Integral cohomology of BU(n)

items.proof_plan: Identify BU(1)=CP∞ with K(Z,2), and use bundle classification plus representability to obtain the natural bijection. The universal c1 is the integral generator by the projective-bundle normalization. On CP∞×CP∞, Kunneth makes H² free on the two coordinate generators; the tensor product of universal lines restricts to the universal line on either axis, so naturality forces its c1 to be their sum. Pullback proves that tensor product corresponds to addition for every allowed base.
items.statement: Assume AC. For every CW complex X, and more generally every paracompact Hausdorff CGWH space having CW homotopy type, c_1:Pic_top(X)→H²(X;Z) is a natural group isomorphism, with tensor product corresponding to addition.
items.title: The first Chern class classifies complex line bundles

items.proof_plan: Use the Picard group isomorphism, L⊗L*=1, and the metric-induced complex-linear isomorphism from the conjugate line to L*.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §4, first-Chern tensor formula, printed pp. 211–212
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. For complex lines, c_1(L⊗M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M), c_1(L^*)=−c_1(L), and the first Chern class of the conjugate line is −c_1(L).
items.title: First Chern class of tensor, dual, and conjugate lines

items.proof_plan: After splitting, both are the product of line Euler classes; descend by integral injectivity and retain the complex orientation.
items.statement: Assume AC. For complex rank-n E with its complex orientation, c_n(E)=e(E_R).
items.title: Top Chern class equals Euler class of the underlying real bundle

items.proof_plan: Split into lines; each underlying oriented real plane has w1=0 and w2=ρ2e=ρ2c1. Multiply and descend using the explicitly supplied F_2-injectivity of the strengthened splitting theorem.
items.statement: Assume AC. For complex E, w_{2i+1}(E_R)=0 and w_{2i}(E_R)=ρ_2c_i(E).
items.title: Mod-two reduction of Chern classes

items.proof_plan: Map v⊗z to v⊗conjugate(z) in the conjugate target. Split V into lines, negate every root, and descend the elementary-symmetric formula.
items.statement: Assume AC. For real E its complexification is canonically complex-linearly isomorphic to its conjugate; for every complex V, conjugation sends c_i(V) to (−1)^ic_i(V).
items.title: Complexification is conjugation invariant

items.proof_plan: Combine E_C≅its conjugate with the odd sign in the conjugation formula.
items.statement: Assume AC. For real E, 2c_{2j+1}(E_C)=0; integral vanishing is not claimed.
items.title: Odd Chern classes of a complexified real bundle are two-torsion

items.proof_plan: Record the complexification, sign, degree, rank cutoff and orientation independence.
items.statement: Assume AC. For real rank-n E define p_i(E)=(−1)^ic_{2i}(E_C)∈H^{4i}(B;Z), with p_0=1 and p_i=0 for 2i>n; no orientation is required.
items.title: Pontryagin classes by complexification

items.proof_plan: Complexification commutes with pullback and trivial sums. Reduce c_{2i}(E_C), identify (E_C)_R≅E⊕E, and read degree 4i from w(E)^2.
items.statement: Assume AC. Pontryagin classes are pullback natural and stable, and ρ_2p_i(E)=w_{2i}(E)^2.
items.title: Naturality, stability, and mod-two reduction of Pontryagin classes

items.proof_plan: Expand the Chern Whitney product, retain even-even terms, and observe every discrepancy contains odd complexification Chern classes killed after inverting two.
items.statement: Assume AC. Over Z[1/2], or any coefficient ring with 2 invertible, p(E⊕F)=p(E)p(F); integrally the omitted odd-Chern cross terms can obstruct this formula.
items.title: Pontryagin Whitney product away from two

items.proof_plan: Identify (E_C)_R with E⊕E. The product and complex orientations differ by (−1)^n; this cancels the defining (−1)^n in p_n and Euler multiplicativity gives e².
items.statement: Assume AC. For oriented real rank-2n E, p_n(E)=e(E)^2 integrally.
items.title: Top Pontryagin class is the square of the Euler class

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the stable classifying-space construction.
items.proof_plan: Model BSO(n) by oriented n-planes in R^∞. A point of the unit-sphere bundle is an oriented n-plane V with a unit vector v∈V; the orthogonal complement v^⊥∩V inherits the unique orientation for which (v,positive basis) is positive. Stable orthogonal transitivity identifies this space with the oriented (n-1)-plane model BSO(n-1), and the projection forgets v. Equivalently it is ESO(n)/SO(n-1)→ESO(n)/SO(n), whose fiber is SO(n)/SO(n-1)=S^{n-1}.

references.locator: Lectures 35–36, universal oriented sphere bundles and BSO induction, printed pp.130–137
references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥2, the unit-sphere bundle of the universal oriented rank-n bundle over BSO(n) is the fibration S^{n-1}→BSO(n-1)→BSO(n), with the total-space identification preserving the induced orientation conventions.
items.title: The universal oriented sphere bundle has BSO(n-1) as total space

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC chooses the simplex lifts used to define transfer simultaneously.
items.proof_plan: For a finite d-sheeted regular cover p:Y→X, lift each singular simplex after choosing one lift and sum its d deck translates; this is a chain map because the full lift-sum is independent of the initial lift. Dualize to transfer tr. Directly on simplices, tr∘p^*=d on H^*(X;Q) and p^*∘tr=Σ_{g∈G}g^* on H^*(Y;Q). Division by d makes p^* injective. Its image is invariant, while an invariant y equals p^*((1/d)tr(y)), proving equality with deck invariants in every degree.

references.locator: §3.G, transfer homomorphisms for finite-sheeted coverings, printed pp.321–326
references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. If p:Y→X is a finite d-sheeted regular covering of CW complexes with deck group G, then p^*:H^*(X;Q)→H^*(Y;Q) is injective and its image is exactly H^*(Y;Q)^G.
items.title: Rational transfer identifies a finite regular cover with deck invariants

items.proof_plan: Use the identified universal sphere bundle and the vector-bundle Gysin sequence inductively, beginning with BSO(1)=*. In odd rank the Euler class is rationally zero; in even rank the Gysin multiplication is by e. Exactness gives the displayed polynomial rings, and the top relation p_m=e² identifies the even-rank square. The forget-orientation map BSO(n)→BO(n) is the regular two-sheeted cover obtained from the oriented Grassmannian. Apply rational transfer: orientation reversal fixes each p_i and negates e, so the invariant subrings are exactly the displayed BO rings.
items.statement: Assume AC. For m≥1, H^*(BO(2m);Q)=H^*(BO(2m+1);Q)=Q[p_1,…,p_m], H^*(BSO(2m+1);Q)=Q[p_1,…,p_m], and H^*(BSO(2m);Q)=Q[p_1,…,p_{m-1},e], with p_m=e². Also BO(0), BSO(0), and BSO(1) are points and have rational cohomology Q.
items.title: Rational cohomology of BO and BSO by Pontryagin and Euler classes

items.proof_plan: The cellular cochain complex of a finite CW complex is concentrated in degrees at most the dimension, and cellular cochains compute singular cohomology with the trivial local system.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a CW pair (X,A) with X finite of dimension d and any coefficient ring R, H^n(X,A;R)=0 for n>d; in particular H^n(X;R)=0 above the dimension.
items.title: Cohomology of a finite CW complex vanishes above its dimension

items.proof_plan: Symmetric-polynomial theory descends the root expression uniquely; finite dimension makes each evaluated total degree finite.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a complex vector bundle E over a finite CW complex X, define ch(E)=Σexp(t_i) in the direct sum H^{even}(X;Q); each homogeneous term is the corresponding rational Newton polynomial in c_1,…,c_n, and finite dimension leaves only finitely many nonzero evaluated terms.
items.title: Chern character of a complex vector bundle

items.proof_plan: On a common splitting space, sums concatenate roots and tensors replace them by t_i+u_j; exponential identities prove both formulas, then injectivity and Grothendieck universality finish. Naturality and the internal product on X×Y then give the external formula ch(a external-product b)=ch(a) external-product ch(b) by writing the external product as the product of the two projection pullbacks.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §4, Chern-character construction and ring-homomorphism lemma, printed pp. 211–212
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite CW complex X, the Chern character is natural, additive on sums and multiplicative on tensors, hence extends uniquely through Grothendieck completion to a unital ring map ch:K^0(X)→H^{even}(X;Q).
items.title: Chern character is a natural ring homomorphism on K-zero

items.proof_plan: Construct the reduced and odd maps before the graded map; iterate Bott and check independence of the even shift using the Bott normalization. For products, use the external-product formula in degree zero. Represent each odd class by a reduced degree-zero class on a suspension; the product diagram uses ΣX_+ smash ΣY_+ isomorphic to Σ²(X×Y)_+, and desuspension by the Bott class. The normalization ch(beta)=the rational S² suspension generator makes this diagram commute. The sphere twist supplies the same Koszul sign in K-theory and cohomology, so even-even, even-odd, and odd-odd external products are all preserved; diagonal pullback gives the internal Z/2-graded product.
items.statement: Assume AC. For an unbased finite CW complex X, subtract rank to get reduced ch and define odd ch through K^{-1}(X)=K~^0(ΣX_+) and reduced cohomology suspension; for based reduced theory use K~^{-1}(X)=K~^0(ΣX). Bott periodicity, normalized on the Bott generator, then gives ch:K^j(X)→⊕_kH^{j+2k}(X;Q). These maps commute with external products and hence with the internal Z/2-graded products.
items.title: Graded Chern character by suspension and Bott periodicity

items.proof_plan: Apply the based character to X/A. A class vanishing on X^{p-1} lifts relatively; its character remains relative and therefore restricts to zero on that skeleton.
items.statement: Assume AC. For finite CW pairs, the graded character gives maps on relative groups commuting with connecting maps and sends the K-theory skeletal filtration F^p into the ordinary-cohomology filtration F^p.
items.title: The graded Chern character respects relative maps and skeletal filtrations

items.proof_plan: Map every skeletal pair. On quotient sphere wedges the Bott normalization sends the K coefficient generator to the rational generator, so E1 and E2 are coefficientwise isomorphisms.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite CW complex, after tensoring with Q the filtered character induces an AHSS morphism whose E2 coefficient map is K^q(*)⊗Q≅Q for even q and zero-to-zero for odd q.
items.title: Chern character induces the rational isomorphism on AHSS E-two

items.proof_plan: E2 comparison gives E∞ comparison. Identify it with gr(ch), then lift through the finite filtration by short exact sequences and the five lemma; rational collapse alone is not used to identify filtered groups. The preceding graded construction already proves multiplicativity in all parity combinations, so the additive bijections in the two parity classes together are a bijective Z/2-graded ring homomorphism.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §4, Chern character and statement of the finite-CW rational isomorphism, printed pp. 211–212
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. For every finite CW complex X and every integer j, ch⊗Q:K^j(X)⊗Q→⊕_kH^{j+2k}(X;Q) is a natural filtered additive isomorphism. Taken over both parity classes, these maps form an isomorphism of Z/2-graded rings.
items.title: Rational Chern character isomorphism for finite CW complexes

title: Chern and Pontryagin Classes by Splitting and Complexification

items.proof_plan: Identify the hyperplane line with γ* and apply the dual-line formula with the fixed cellular orientation.
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥1, tautological γ over CP^n and the positive generator x=c_1(γ^*) satisfy c_1(γ)=−x and c(γ^*)=1+x.
items.title: Chern class of tautological and hyperplane lines on complex projective space

items.proof_plan: Iterate line normalization and the Whitney product, then take homogeneous components.
items.statement: Assume AC. On (CP∞)^n, for E=⊕L_i and x_i=c_1(L_i), c(E)=∏(1+x_i) and c_k is the kth elementary symmetric polynomial.
items.title: Chern classes of a sum of universal complex lines

items.proof_plan: The circle fundamental-group theorem and the power-map degree calculation identify the clutching map z↦z^d with d times the Hopf clutching generator. The published Hopf-line calculation fixes the d=1 bundle and orientation. The c1 classification is a group isomorphism, so tensor/clutching addition sends the class to d·u, including negative d and d=0.
items.statement: Assume AC. For d∈Z and the positive generator u∈H²(S²;Z) fixed by the Hopf orientation, the line over S² clutched by z↦z^d has c_1=d·u; clutching degree and first Chern number give the same Z-classification.
items.title: Complex line bundles over the two-sphere by clutching degree

items.proof_plan: Specialize the top-Chern/Euler and mod-two comparison theorems to rank one with complex orientation.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a complex line L, e(L_R)=c_1(L), w_1(L_R)=0, and w_2(L_R)=ρ_2c_1(L).
items.title: Realification of a complex line compares c-one, w-two, and Euler

items.proof_plan: Use total class one for a trivial summand, the stability formulas, and the defining rank cutoffs.
items.statement: Assume AC. For trivial ε^r, c(E⊕ε^r)=c(E) and p(F⊕ε^r)=p(F); c_i vanishes above complex rank and p_i when 2i exceeds real rank.
items.title: Stability and rank cutoff under adding a trivial summand

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the characteristic-class and projective-space suppliers.
items.proof_plan: For the universal line the rank-one real projective-bundle definition identifies w_1(λ) with the tautological class u. The underlying real bundle of λ_C is canonically λ⊕λ via v⊗(a+ib)↦(av,bv). Mod-two Chern reduction and Whitney multiplication therefore give ρ_2(a)=w_2(λ⊕λ)=u². The polynomial ring H^*(RP^∞;F_2)=F_2[u] makes u^{2k} nonzero, so ρ_2(a^k)=u^{2k}≠0. The odd-Chern complexification theorem gives 2a=0, hence 2a^k=0; nonzero reduction shows every a^k is a nonzero class of exact order two.

references.locator: Lecture 36, complexification and the two-torsion obstruction to integral Pontryagin multiplication, printed pp.134–137
references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.statement: Assume AC. Let λ be the universal real line on RP^∞, u=w_1(λ), and a=c_1(λ_C). Then 2a=0, ρ_2(a)=u², and for every k≥1 the class a^k is nonzero of exact order two with ρ_2(a^k)=u^{2k}.
items.title: Integral powers of the complexified universal real line

items.proof_plan: The preceding lemma proves a²≠0 with no appeal to an additive UCT calculation. Since E_C=λ_C⊕λ_C, Whitney multiplication gives c_2(E_C)=a² and therefore p_1(E)=-a²≠0. Every positive p_i(λ) vanishes by the real-rank cutoff, so p(λ)p(λ)=1.
items.statement: Assume AC. For the universal real line λ over RP∞ and E=λ⊕λ, p_1(E)=−a²≠0 for a=c_1(λ_C) of order two, while p(λ)p(λ)=1 by rank cutoff.
items.title: Integral total Pontryagin multiplicativity cannot ignore two-torsion

title: Chern and Pontryagin Classes by Splitting and Complexification — Examples
